subject: FintechCo pricing & residency - follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Stone <alex.stone@fintechco.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 14:05:12 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps — pricing + residency clarification

Alex — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery and a suggested next step list so we can get you a clean proposal: 

Summary of needs:
- Workloads: conversational NLU + document summarization for payments ops. Estimated steady-state: ~5M tokens/month for NLU, additional ~2M tokens/month for summaries (total ~7M). Peak/seasonal spikes up to 15M in high days.
- Residency: payments-related data needs EU residency; non-payments can be processed in US.
- SLA: 99.9% availability desired, audit logs + SOC2 required.

Questions / open items for you to confirm:
1) Can you confirm the approximate monthly token volume band (we used 5–10M for today's calc)?
2) What is the target budget range you’re considering for the LLM service (monthly)? You mentioned exploring mid-market procurement bands.
3) Any strict timeline for going live in EU region?

Pricing / unit-economics note (high-level):
- Regional pricing can vary — EU region typically carries a premium due to infra and data residency (we typically see ~10–15% higher unit costs).
- For a public-cloud hosted model, baseline list runs around $1,000 per 1M tokens in US on our hosted tier; EU would be roughly $1,120/1M in the same tier (ballpark). Committed/annual terms reduce that by 10–15%.

Attachments: pricing-worksheet.xlsx (initial worksheet), residency-faq.pdf (residency/controls summary).

Next steps:
- Alex: can you confirm volumes & target budget band?
- I’ll follow up with a modeled pricing example (US vs EU) and a suggested commitment tier that gives the best unit economics for your volumes.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — pricing + residency clarification

Thanks Marissa — good summary. A few clarifications from our side (quick):

- Volumes: our initial pilot (Q3) targets roughly 5M tokens/month on conversational traffic (as you wrote). If pilot performs, we expect growth to ~25M tokens/month within 6–9 months (mainly driven by increased customer interaction rates).
- Budget: for pilot we have a target range of $8k–$15k/month. For scale we would re-evaluate.
- Residency: Payments data must remain in EU. Non-payments (support messages, marketing) can be processed in US. So ideally we want a split routing option or EU-only for payments workflows.
- Target unit-economics: we’re trying to aim for <= $1,200 per 1M tokens initially. Lower is obviously better. Can you surface both list and committed pricing for US vs EU (and any suggestions for dedicated vs hosted to meet EU residency)?

I’ve cc’ed procurement and our security lead (Lena) who will have follow-up on audit logs + controls.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.
— Alex
Alex Stone
Head of Product, FintechCo
alex.stone@fintechco.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Stone <alex.stone@fintechco.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Procurement <procurement@fintechco.com>, Lena Park <lena.park@fintechco.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 09:10:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — pricing + residency clarification

Alex — great, thanks for the detail. Below is a concise pricing model (ballpark) and a couple recommended deployment patterns given your residency needs. I’m attaching an updated worksheet with scenarios.

High-level unit economics (hosted API, per 1M tokens)
- US hosted (list): $1,000 / 1M tokens
- EU hosted (list): $1,120 / 1M tokens (approx +12% premium)
- Committed 12-mo (US): $850 / 1M tokens (15% discount off US list)
- Committed 12-mo (EU): $960 / 1M tokens (approx 14% discount off EU list)

Example math (pilot 5M tokens/mo):
- US hosted list: 5 * $1,000 = $5,000/mo
- EU hosted list: 5 * $1,120 = $5,600/mo
- Committed 12-mo US: 5 * $850 = $4,250/mo (saves $750/mo vs list)

Deployment suggestions for residency:
1) EU-only for payments flows: route payments-related calls to EU-hosted model endpoints. That gives you residency with minimal change to app routing. This is what most customers choose when only a subset of data requires EU residency.
2) Dedicated/Private for full EU control: if you want the strongest controls and to avoid cross-region dependencies, Redwood Dedicated or Private deployment in your EU VPC is recommended (higher baseline cost but predictable performance and stronger isolation).

Tradeoffs:
- EU hosted (multi-tenant) is fastest to get started; small premium and standard SOC2/audit logs.
- Dedicated/Private reduces per-call compute overhead (depending on commit) and simplifies compliance, but requires a procurement/commit conversation (we can model TCO).

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll send a modeled worksheet showing US vs EU hosted vs dedicated TCO for projected 5M, 15M, 25M tokens/month (attached).
- Sean will confirm if we have any special enterprise pricing levers for EU residency in this deal.

Let me know if you want a short follow-up call this week to walk through the worksheet.

Thanks — Marissa
[Attachment: updated-pricing-worksheet.xlsx (xlsx)]

+1 on Marissa's approach. A few internal notes and what I can confirm to the customer: 

- We can offer EU-hosted residency for payments with the pricing Marissa listed. If they move to a 12-month committed tier we can take another 5% off the EU committed rate for deals above $60k ARR — I’ll confirm exact thresholds but we usually structure as a stepped commit.
- Dedicated capacity / private deployments: we’ll need procurement engagement (longer lead time) but we can model a blended unit cost that can be competitive at scale. Recommend we include a side-by-side TCO in the proposal.
- Security: SOC2+audit logs are standard on dedicated/private; for EU hosted we can provide the audit artifacts and data locality assurances — Lena, we can follow up with a short checklist.

Marissa — I’ll help finalize the proposal and work through commit thresholds. Alex — expect a formal modeled proposal by EOD Wednesday if you can confirm volumes/budget band.

— Sean
